summary: Permission propagation delay prevents access to internal QueryHub DB tool
description:
Issue summary: Several engineers report 403 / Access Denied when trying to open QueryHub immediately after an AdminUI role grant.

Impact: ~8 engineers across analytics and infra teams could not run ad-hoc queries for ~30-45 minutes; blocked debug and release validation work. No customer-facing outage but blocked engineer productivity.

Environment: prod - us-west (QueryHub behind auth-proxy v2; rbac-service v1.9; identity-sync consumer reading Okta SCIM webhooks).

Steps to reproduce:
1) AdminUI: grant user the QueryHub role (queryhub:read) and save.
2) User logs out of the webapp and logs back in via Okta SSO.
3) QueryHub shows 403 and logs show missing claim group.

Observed behaviour: Role grants appear in Okta System Log immediately, but QueryHub access is denied for a delayed window (~30-45 minutes). rbac-service reports stale group membership until a manual resync.

Relevant logs / traces:
- Okta System Log entries: group.add for users (timestamped show success)
- identity-sync consumer metrics (CloudWatch): consumer lag spike, repeated 500s on SCIM webhook handler between 2026-03-13T14:05 and 14:20 UTC
- auth-proxy logs: repeated 403 with X-Auth-Claim: groups missing "queryhub:read"
- rbac-service: last membership reconciliation for affected users "2026-03-13T14:02:12Z"

Related links:
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/abc123/identity-sync?orgId=1 (consumer lag graph)
- Kibana: https://kibana.redwood.company/app/kibana#/discover/identity-sync-logs (SCIM webhook 500s)
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01234567/p1678780200000000

investigation_notes:
Timeline and checks performed:
- Confirmed Okta group add events are logged immediately for affected users.
- Observed identity-sync consumer lag (SQS depth) and repeated 500s from SCIM webhook handler; root cause: intermittent upstream timeout to Okta endpoint when identity-sync retried bulk operations.
- rbac-service caches membership state for 15 minutes; cache wasn't invalidated during the backlog window which amplified propagation delay.
- Temporarily cleared SQS backlog and restarted identity-sync workers which allowed pending webhooks to be processed; rbac-service then reconciled membership.
Hypothesis: A short-lived Okta API latency spike caused SCIM pushes to be retried and queued, combined with rbac-service cache TTL meant new grants were not visible until reconciliation.
Actions taken during investigation:
- Restarted identity-sync workers (Marcos)
- Triggered manual reconciliation on rbac-service for affected users (Janelle)
- Confirmed QueryHub access restored for all reported users
- Correlated with Grafana and Kibana graphs; no other services impacted.
resolution:
Workaround: For immediate unblocking we triggered a manual rbac-service reconciliation for affected users and cleared a short SQS backlog; this restored access within ~5 minutes.
Permanent fix: Deployed identity-sync hotfix to add exponential backoff/retry and to emit webhook error-rate metrics; reduced default rbac-service cache TTL from 15m to 2m for group membership lookups and added a cache invalidation hook on successful SCIM processing.
Follow-ups: (1) Create alert: SCIM webhook 5xx rate > 1% within 5m (ticket created INT-126790). (2) Add a canary test in CI that simulates a role grant and asserts propagation within 2 minutes. (3) Documented runbook steps for manual reconciliation in Confluence.
Status: Resolved (hotfix deployed to prod us-west and validated by reproducing a role grant test).
